intro: Review how integration and E2E tests protect against regressions.

questions.prompt: Why do integration tests provide more protection against regressions than unit tests?

options.text: They run faster and cover less logic.
They cover multiple components and out-of-process dependencies
They cover the entire system, so they replace E2E tests.
They mock every dependency to provide complete isolation.
They cover every logical branch in a use case.

questions.prompt: Why do E2E tests offer the strongest protection against bugs?

options.text: They run only pure in-memory functions with no external effects.
They run the full application as the user experiences it, including real APIs, databases, and external systems.
They need less setup and are easier to maintain than integration tests.

questions.prompt: Which scenario is best suited to an E2E test?

options.text: Check whether the createQuizModel function trims whitespace.
Check quiz creation with fake adapters and stubbed network responses.
Check whether isolated UI components render correctly in Storybook.
Verify that an authenticated user can create a quiz through the full application.
